title: Progressive spec-reduction admission controller with priority-aware token budgets
creator: Luca Ortiz
description:
Problem: During regional capacity spikes and multi-region failovers we observe SLO burn driven by long-tail token costs and queue saturation. Simple global shedding causes unfair tenant impact and noisy user-facing errors.

Proposal: Implement a Tiered Admission Controller that performs progressive "spec-reduction" on accepted requests instead of blunt rejection when capacity is constrained. The controller composes three mechanisms: priority-aware token budgets, admission gating with soft-fallback windows, and response-spec reduction transforms (token trimming, schema-elision, and partial-field folding). The controller integrates with existing circuit breakers and multi-region failover logic so that fallbacks are deterministic (e.g., route to compatible model variant or reveal degraded response).

Key capabilities: 
- Tenant priority lanes with proportional token budgets and borrow windows.
- Admission gating that assigns requests to one of: FastPath (full fidelity), SlimPath (quantized model + token trim), FoldPath (structured response elision + partial answers), or Reject (last resort).
- Spec-reduction transforms: prefix-preserving truncation, slot-level elision (remove low-value structured fields), and response folding (return condensed summary plus pointer to async fetch).
- Graceful degrade policies per route: config-driven fidelity ladder, SLO-preserving thresholds (SLO burn, p95 latency headroom, token-credits).
- Observability hooks: per-tenant fallback rate, per-path latency/cost, successful/failed foldbacks, and synthetic prompt regressions.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Under synthetic spike tests (2x baseline QPS), system keeps p95 below SLO for 90% of tenants and reduces reject rate by >= 60% compared to baseline shedding.
- Fallback rate per tenant < 10% in normal load, and documented quality delta metrics for SlimPath and FoldPath.
- Rollout plan: feature-flagged, gradual ramp per region, canary with 5% tenants, telemetry gating and automatic rollback on SLO burn > 5% for a 1h window.

Why different from existing shedding approaches: Focus is on controlled fidelity reduction at the response/schema level (not only queue eviction or token-limit truncation) and a tenant-borrowing model to reduce unfair halting of lower-priority but critical tenants.

Trade-offs & risks: 
- Increased runtime complexity (transform plumbing + model variant routing).
- Potential for user confusion if degraded responses are not clearly annotated. Requires UX/SDK signals to callers.
- Observability and regression testing requirements are non-trivial (need synthetic prompt sets and quality checks).
comments: 2025-02-21: Initial design review with Priya (SRE) and Owen (Runtime). Agreement to prototype spec-reduction transforms as middleware to avoid runtime hot-path regressions.

2025-02-25: Spike results: implementing token-budget accounting as an in-memory leaky bucket per tenant is feasible. Observed 8% overhead on admission path in microbenchmarks (P95 added latency +1.4ms). Action: move heavy transforms to lightweight pre-accept stage and async enrichment when possible.

2025-02-28: Design decision: three fidelity tiers (Full, Slim, Fold) mapped to configurable token budgets and model-variant compatibility. PM accepted UX requirement to include 'degraded' metadata in responses for tracing and SDK helpers.

2025-03-03: Integration prototype PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2412. Includes token-budget middleware, admission gate, and two transform implementations (slot-elide, prefix-trim). Seeking review from Owen and Priya.

2025-03-04: Load test (region eu-west-1) with synthetic tenants (1000 tenants, 2x spike). Preliminary: reject rate down 64%, average tokens consumed down 28% for SlimPath, FoldPath quality delta measured via eval set: ROUGE-L drop ~6% on summaries. Need PM signoff on quality tolerances.

2025-03-05: Security review note: transforms touch user payloads and may alter PII surfaces. Security asked for a short audit; scope added as dependency. Added KMS tagging check for any persisted partial results.
Next steps: finish PR reviews, add SDK flags for 'accept_degraded_responses', add full telemetry dashboards, and schedule canary in us-central-1 for 2025-03-18.
